eta in (0,1/beta]; alpha eta<=beta eta<=1 and eta>0.
pi_eta(dx dy) proportional exp(-V(x)-||x-y||^2/(2eta))dxdy.
X~mu; independent standard Gaussian Z; Y=X+sqrt(eta)Z.
Real Hilbert L2 of a probability measure consists of ae measurable square-integrable equivalence classes; real inner product int fg; centered subspace int f=0.
Closed subspace and unique bounded orthogonal projection P_M; f-P_M f lies in orthogonal complement.
Operators in analysis bounded linear unless stated; adjoint, selfadjointness, norm contraction, unitary, selfadjoint involution; Loewner order via all real quadratic forms.
Spectral theorem for selfadjoint bounded operators; nonnegative operator has a unique nonnegative square root.
P f = conditional expectation given Y; depends on y; bounded orthogonal projection on H=L2(pi_eta).
H_P=ran(P), y-only observables; H_perp=ker(P)=ran(I-P), conditional-zero-mean; orthogonal direct decomposition.
T_ab=P_a T P_b as maps H_b -> H_a; first index target, second source.
U f(x,y)=f(x,2x-y); pullback selfadjoint unitary and involutive.
C=U_PP=P U P on H_P is selfadjoint contraction; A=U_perpP=Pperp U P maps H_P to H_perp; offdiagonal adjoint.
U^2=I in blocks gives A* A=I-C^2 and A* U_perpperp=-C A*.
Y+=X+sqrt(eta)Z; Y-=X-sqrt(eta)Z; pair exchangeable; H_P identified with L2(pi_eta^Y).
Gamma_P=(I-C^2)^(1/2) on H_P, nonnegative branch specified by D.1. No inverse used in definition.
From B.5 and Gamma definition: A* A=Gamma_P^2 and ||A f||=||Gamma_P f|| for every f in H_P; squares give energy ||f||^2-||C f||^2.
Under beta eta<=1, rho=(1-alpha eta)/(1+alpha eta); gamma=sqrt(1-rho^2)=2sqrt(alpha eta)/(1+alpha eta), gamma>=sqrt(alpha eta)/2.
Density proportional exp(-V((y+u)/2)-||y-u||^2/(8eta)); s_y=-(1/2)grad V((y+u)/2)-(y-u)/(4eta); differentiating normalized density gives gradient C f = conditional covariance.
C.1 covariance, conditional Poincare/Cauchy-Schwarz and Hessian bound -> C.2; marginal Poincare C.3 plus C.2 -> ||C f||<=rho||f|| on centered H_P,0.
H_P,0=H_P intersect L2_0(pi_eta); C preserves it because C is selfadjoint and preserves constants.
On H_P,0, ||C||<=rho implies Gamma_P>=gamma I via positive functional calculus; inverse is bounded only on this centered subspace.
Restricted Gamma inverse gives A=V Gamma, V=A Gamma^-1:H_P,0->H_perp and V*V=I. This is a downstream consumer outside current root/compression/leakage/energy/uniqueness proof unit.
